Casio and G-Shock.name: G-Shock 5600
Casio and G-Shock.movement: Quartz; solar and radio-synced on GW-M5610U
Casio and G-Shock.desc: The original square G-Shock, nearly indestructible, and the solar radio version never needs a battery or time setting.

Casio and G-Shock.name: G-Shock GA-2100
Casio and G-Shock.desc: Thin octagonal analog-digital G-Shock nicknamed the CasiOak, tough and light with a look borrowed from luxury sports watches.

Casio and G-Shock.name: Duro MDV-106
Casio and G-Shock.desc: A real 200m dive watch with a rotating bezel for well under the price of a dinner out.

Casio and G-Shock.name: F-91W and A168
Casio and G-Shock.desc: Cheap classic Casio digitals with alarm, stopwatch and light, famous for lasting years on one battery.

Orient.name: Bambino
Orient.desc: Domed-crystal automatic dress watch that is the usual first recommendation for a cheap mechanical dress watch.

Orient.name: Kamasu
Orient.desc: Affordable 200m automatic diver with a scratch-resistant sapphire crystal and many dial colours; a GMT version now exists.

Orient.name: Mako 40
Orient.desc: Smaller, modern take on Orient's classic Mako diver with sapphire crystal and 200m water resistance.

Orient.name: Sun and Moon
Orient.desc: Dressy automatic with a small rotating sun and moon disc showing day or night, sold in Bambino and Stretto cases.

Seiko.name: Seiko 5 Sports
Seiko.desc: Seiko's everyday automatic sports watch in countless colours, the classic entry point to mechanical watches; GMT versions sit at the top.

Seiko.name: Presage Cocktail Time
Seiko.desc: Dress watch with glossy textured dials inspired by cocktails, offering showroom-level shine at a modest price.

Seiko.name: Prospex Turtle
Seiko.desc: Cushion-cased 200m dive watch revived from a 1970s Seiko, known for comfort and toughness.

Seiko.name: Prospex Alpinist
Seiko.desc: Compact field watch with a compass bezel and a long 70 hour power reserve, originally made for Japanese mountaineers.

Seiko.name: Prospex 1965 Heritage Diver
Seiko.desc: Modern remake of Seiko's first dive watch, often called the best all-round diver around this price.

Seagull.name: 1963 Chronograph
Seagull.desc: Reissue of a 1963 Chinese air force chronograph, the cheapest way to own a proper mechanical column-wheel chronograph.

Seagull.name: Ocean Star
Seagull.desc: Seagull's sapphire-crystal automatic diver, a solid budget alternative to Japanese divers.

Seagull.name: 819 Dress
Seagull.movement: Automatic or hand-wound, in-house ST2130 / ST17
Seagull.desc: Classic dress watches with blued hands and display backs, offering fine finishing for little money.

Zelos.name: Swordfish
Zelos.desc: Zelos's signature bold dive watch in steel, titanium and coated cases, often in limited colour drops.

Zelos.name: Mako
Zelos.desc: Higher-spec 300m and 500m diver, including GMT models, sold in small launch batches.

Laco.name: Pilot Watch Basic (Aachen, Augsburg)
Laco.desc: German WWII-style pilot watch with a huge readable dial, the cheapest way into a real Flieger from a historic maker.

Laco.name: Pilot Watch Original (Erbstück)
Laco.desc: Laco's faithful recreations of its 1940s pilot watches, with aged Erbstück versions that look like heirlooms.

Laco.name: Squad (Atlantik, Himalaya, Mojave)
Laco.desc: Rugged modern tool watches with sandwich dials and strong water resistance, built for outdoor use.

Brew.name: Metric
Brew.desc: Compact 1970s-style chronograph inspired by espresso machines, with a quartz movement that has a snappy mechanical-feel stopwatch.

Brew.name: Super Metric
Brew.desc: Retro Metric with a more elaborate dial built around timing a perfect espresso shot.

Brew.name: Retromatic
Brew.desc: Brew's automatic three-hander in the same cushion case, with a simple time-and-date dial.

Brew.name: Retrograph
Brew.desc: Brew's earlier 1970s chronograph design that built the brand's following.

Helm.name: Vanuatu
Helm.desc: Chunky, over-built dive watch sold on a waiting list, prized for heavy-duty build at a low price.

Helm.name: Khuraburi
Helm.desc: ISO-rated diver with a sapphire crystal, a lot of watch for around $300.

Helm.name: Komodo
Helm.desc: Sturdy dive watch now also offered in lightweight titanium.

Helm.name: Miyako
Helm.desc: Helm's dive design with a smoother Miyota 9000-series movement, offered with or without date.

Mr Jones Watches.name: A Perfectly Useless Afternoon
Mr Jones Watches.desc: A playful watch with no hands, just a beach scene and a drink that rotate to show the time.

Mr Jones Watches.name: A Perfectly Useless Morning
Mr Jones Watches.desc: Companion design where a coffee cup and toast tell the time, an easy conversation starter.

Mr Jones Watches.name: The Accurate
Mr Jones Watches.desc: Witty art watch with words in place of hands, typical of the brand's tongue-in-cheek London designs.

Smiths.name: Everest PRS-25
Smiths.desc: Homage to the watch worn on the first Everest ascent, a simple go-anywhere explorer sold in small batches.

Smiths.name: Baby Willard PRS-68
Smiths.desc: Revival of a 1970s cushion-case diver with chunky lume, sold in occasional drops.

Smiths.name: W.W.W. PRS-59
Smiths.desc: Military field watch modelled on British army watches of the 1940s.

Scurfa.name: Diver One
Scurfa.desc: Simple, very tough quartz dive watch designed by a working commercial diver, often sold out within minutes.

Scurfa.name: Bell Diver 1
Scurfa.desc: Scurfa's automatic diver with a no-nonsense tool design and high water resistance.

Scurfa.name: Treasure Seeker
Scurfa.desc: Vintage-styled automatic dive watch, Scurfa's dressier option.

Vostok.name: Amphibia
Vostok.desc: Soviet-era diver with a clever seal that tightens under pressure, a cult favourite for under $200.

Vostok.name: Komandirskie
Vostok.desc: Military commander's watch from Russia, cheap, tough and full of Soviet character.

Tissot.name: PRX
Tissot.desc: 1970s-style integrated-bracelet sports watch that made the luxury look affordable, with an 80 hour automatic movement.

Tissot.name: Seastar 1000
Tissot.desc: Swiss 300m dive watch with an 80 hour power reserve, a value alternative to bigger-name divers.

Tissot.name: Gentleman
Tissot.desc: Versatile steel everyday watch with an anti-magnetic silicon hairspring, dressy enough for an office.

Tissot.name: PRC 200
Tissot.desc: Sporty steel quartz chronograph with a stopwatch, a reliable Swiss watch at a low price.

Tissot.name: Le Locle
Tissot.desc: Traditional dress watch with Roman numerals and guilloche dial, named after Tissot's hometown.

Hamilton.name: Khaki Field Mechanical
Hamilton.desc: Simple army-style field watch you wind by hand, one of the best-loved first Swiss watches.

Hamilton.name: Khaki Field Murph
Hamilton.desc: Field watch made famous by the film Interstellar, clean dial with an 80 hour automatic movement.

Hamilton.name: Khaki Navy Scuba
Hamilton.desc: Colourful, sporty Swiss dive watch rated to 100m, an easy everyday diver.

Hamilton.name: Khaki Aviation Pilot Day Date
Hamilton.desc: Large, highly readable pilot watch showing both day and date.

Hamilton.name: Jazzmaster
Hamilton.desc: Hamilton's dressier range, including open-heart dials that show the movement through the front.

Hamilton.name: Ventura
Hamilton.desc: Triangular 1957 design, the world's first electric watch shape and famously worn by Elvis.

Certina.name: DS Action Diver
Certina.desc: Proper ISO-rated Swiss dive watch with an 80 hour movement; the 38mm size suits smaller wrists.

Certina.name: DS PH200M
Certina.desc: Faithful remake of Certina's 1960s dive watch, vintage looks with modern reliability.

Certina.name: DS Super PH500M
Certina.desc: Chunky 500m reissue of a 1960s professional diver with a distinctive cushion case.

Certina.name: DS-7
Certina.desc: Certina's everyday steel sports watch on a bracelet, built around the brand's shock-resistant Double Security case.

Mido.name: Ocean Star 39
Mido.desc: Compact, vintage-inspired 200m diver with an 80 hour movement, a well-sized everyday Swiss diver.

Mido.name: Multifort TV Big Date
Mido.desc: Retro TV-screen shaped case with a big date display and a certified accurate movement.

Mido.name: Ocean Star 200C
Mido.desc: Modern 200m diver with a ceramic bezel that resists scratching and fading.

Mido.name: Baroncelli
Mido.desc: Thin, classic dress watch line, a good-value Swiss formal watch.

Mido.name: Commander
Mido.desc: Mid-century styled steel watch first made in 1959, with a distinctive tough monobloc case.
